record.body: Signature frog-chorus analogues are invented night choruses in which several designed caller types call together, each with its own pulse rate and pitch band so that listeners can separate them. The design includes a temperature rule, borrowed as an idea from real frogs, in which pulse rate rises with temperature, but the numbers are design choices, not measurements from any real pond. A Signature chorus can be simulated by adding its caller types together, and the pair's demo programs do exactly that in arithmetic. This record covers the Signature biophony layer, distinct from Signature geophony such as designed rain and Signature anthrophony such as designed road noise.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Frog-Chorus Analogues: Designed Night Choruses'
N = 25
SEC = 1
DUR = 3.0
per_sec = N / SEC
per_min = per_sec * 60.0
duty = N * DUR / SEC
total = per_sec * DUR
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Count: %d in %d seconds' % (N, SEC))
print('Rate: %.2f per second, %.2f per minute' % (per_sec, per_min))
print('Duty cycle: %.3f' % duty)
print('Total in one call of %.1f seconds: %.1f' % (DUR, total))
demo.expected_output:
Record: Signature Frog-Chorus Analogues: Designed Night Choruses
Count: 25 in 1 seconds
Rate: 25.00 per second, 1500.00 per minute
Duty cycle: 75.000
Total in one call of 3.0 seconds: 75.0

record.math_proof: Math proof: a Signature caller at 25 pulses per second for 3 seconds produces 25 x 3 = 75 pulses per call.
record.science_proof: Science proof: the design mirrors the real chorus principle that species-specific pulse rates let listeners separate mixed choruses, applied here to invented caller types with stated pulse rates.
